notes_for_editor: Thin record. The register gives type 'Unk' and nothing else, so the story does not say the site was a tower; the brief's kind 'unknown' stands. The TSHA entry is about the community, not the lookout, and it does not mention a tower. A Shelby County Today column by Neal Murphy (https://scttx.com/articles/fire-towers-neal-murphy) describes a fire tower just west of San Augustine on CR280 that is now gone. It is not used here because the column gives no coordinates and places the tower at San Augustine, not White City; it may describe the San Augustine record instead. A Portal to Texas History search for "White City" "fire tower" returned 18 newspaper items, none of which showed the phrase in its cached page text, so none is cited. No build date, height, agency, staffing or fire record found. Story body is 107 words after the fact-check. It stays short because no source describes the lookout, and no claim was added to reach 120 words. The word 'small' was removed because the TSHA entry does not call the community small. The Unk sentence now carries its own footnote.
